lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: precise definitions of angle, circle, line, and segment
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: precise definitions of angle, circle, line, and segment

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

steps: Fix a centre and a distance.
Take every point in the plane at that distance.
workedSolution.answer: the set of points at a fixed distance from a centre

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. With the compass set to the radius, mark successive arcs around the circle from a starting point, then join consecutive marks. What has been constructed?
choices: an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle
a regular pentagon inscribed in the circle
a square inscribed in the circle
a regular hexagon inscribed in the circle

items.prompt: A regular triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 8. What central angle does each side subtend?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly justifies the perpendicular bisector construction?
choices: Any line through the midpoint is a perpendicular bisector.
The arcs look symmetric, so the line must be perpendicular.
Both constructed points are equidistant from the endpoints, and the locus of such points is exactly the perpendicular bisector.
The compass width was more than half the segment, which forces perpendicularity.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a parallel lines?
choices: two lines the same distance apart at one point
two lines with the same length
two lines that meet only at infinity
two coplanar lines that never intersect, however far they are extended

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Through point P not on line ℓ, copy the angle that a transversal makes with ℓ, placing the copy at P on the same transversal. What has been constructed?
choices: the reflection of ℓ across P
a line through P perpendicular to ℓ
the perpendicular bisector of the transversal
a line through P parallel to ℓ

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 4. What central angle does each side subtend?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly justifies the equilateral triangle construction on a given segment?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a circle?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
